title: Keep Cargo runtime values and artifact data out of interlockings

facts.note: Validator subject_kind is 'interlocking'; applies to every interlocking, whatever its home and whether or not it is currently compliant. Needs a classifier that recognises interlocking definitions among planner artifacts.

fires: Any interlocking is present in a planner artifact, including one that already complies (the rule still applies; it simply passes).
An interlocking contains Cargo runtime values in some field (applies and fails).
An interlocking contains artifact data in some field (applies and fails).
doesNotFire: Cargo definitions, artifacts or payload contracts themselves, outside any interlocking (different subject).
Plans, wagons, WMBTs or acceptances that contain no interlocking (no subject).

given: A planner artifact contains an interlocking.
when: You write, change or review that interlocking's contents.
then: The interlocking selects routes and declares payload contract identities, and contains no Cargo runtime values and no artifact data.
prefer: Reference each payload by its contract identity and let the route carry the actual Cargo at runtime.
Keep concrete values and artifact content in the Cargo/artifact layer where they are produced.
avoid: Inlining Cargo runtime values (sample or concrete payload values) in any interlocking field.
Copying artifact data into an interlocking to 'document' or pre-fill a route.
Hiding runtime values in nested or renamed fields to dodge the validator.
why: Interlockings are route-selection and contract-identity declarations; putting Cargo runtime values or artifact data in them couples routing to specific payload instances and blurs the boundary between plan and runtime data.
evidence: On failure, the finding reports interlocking_id, field_path and forbidden_value_kind; a clean run has no such findings.
verifier_detail: Validation family: policy; template: forbidden_construct_absence; variant: planner_train_interlocking_does_not_carry_cargo.
